chunks: “Whoever is compelled by necessity to eat from a dead animal, blood, or the flesh of a pig, yet does not eat anything of that until he dies, then he is a disbeliever.”

key_terms.الدَّمِ: blood as a prohibited substance for consumption
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: carrion or an animal dead without lawful slaughter
key_terms.كَافِرٌ: one deemed a disbeliever for rejecting the divine ruling in this context
key_terms.لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: the flesh of swine, normally forbidden to eat

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about refusing forbidden food in a life-threatening necessity?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a person is driven by necessity to consume otherwise haram things such as carrion, blood, or pork, it becomes obligatory to preserve life by eating enough to survive. Refusing that divine concession until death is presented as a rejection of Allah’s ruling, underscoring the sanctity of life and the binding force of lawful necessity in Islamic law.
